method: Each supplied path independently scanned with atomscan --no-update --mode slow --follow=none and cleave facts. Rizin control-flow/call-site review, pefile parsing, Capstone instruction decoding, byte comparisons and independent string-transform reconstruction; no application code executed.
external_evidence: All three supplied tria.ge pages were inaccessible. Verdicts rely on local code; ML verdicts, collector filenames and prior repository review reports do not establish behavior.
shared_loader_evidence: All three outer .text extents, file 0x1000..0x289a, are byte-identical. Native entry VA 0x402674 calls dispatch 0x401cb0. DWORD at file 0x4120 is 3 in each, selecting Active Setup function 0x401900 and cleanup 0x401390.

0x401900 obtains a GUID and the module path, constructs the Active Setup Installed Components key, creates it in HKLM, writes REG_EXPAND_SZ StubPath at 0x401a4b, reads the image with CRT I/O, patches configuration, writes a copy, and calls CreateProcessA at 0x401b7e. In 325 the key and value-name strings are randomized, so the scan correctly does not claim Active Setup or LanmanServer persistence there.

0x401390 calls GetModuleFileNameA and GetShortPathNameA, reads COMSPEC, builds /c del <own-short-path> > nul, starts a shell at 0x4014b8 and resumes its thread. Cleanup belongs to the malicious resource-injector code, not generic shell deletion.

Alternate mode 1 calls resource extractor 0x402460 with type DLL and ID 101. It obtains resource bytes, copies them to an allocation, and calls 0x4023c0 to write the same bytes through CreateFileA/WriteFile. Resource data starts at file 0x5060, length 0x9c00.

0x401260 opens HKLM/SYSTEM/CurrentControlSet/Services/LanmanServer/Parameters, deletes ServiceDLL and writes a replacement expandable SystemRoot/System32/StormServer.dll path at 0x40133e. This is service-DLL configuration hijacking, not DLL search-order resolution.

0x401150 selects an IE/notepad/calc child image, calls CreateProcessA, allocates remote memory, writes the DLL path, resolves Kernel32!LoadLibraryA through GetModuleHandleA/GetProcAddress, and passes that address plus the remote path buffer to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.

Mode 2 includes self-copy, hidden/system attributes, automatic-start service creation at 0x4021de, and service dispatch that extracts and injects the resource DLL. Presence of these paths does not show they were run in mode 3.
intact_payload_evidence: b52 embedded DLL retains its imports and x86 instructions in a writable .data section. PE entry RVA 0x741a reaches 0x10007176. On process attach this creates a mutex, checks ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS and starts a worker at 0x10006922.
The worker calls 0x10006974 repeatedly. That routine resolves the configured host, creates/connects a TCP socket, sends a STORM-formatted host report and calls record receiver 0x10006ac9.

At 0x10006b45 recv reads up to 0x528 bytes. Positive return gates a copy into a stack record; the leading DWORD selects tasks. Task 1 selects flood builders, task 2 stops floods, and other tasks dispatch downloader, UI, removal and shutdown operations. This establishes operator tasking, not merely networking imports.

Raw flood routine 0x1000228e creates WSASocketA(AF_INET=2, SOCK_RAW=3, IPPROTO_UDP=17), sets a socket option and builds the target sockaddr. At 0x10002353 twelve sendto calls repeat per burst, followed by configurable Sleep and return to a stop flag at 0x1000234a. Builders are called from the received attack record and spawn this routine.

Task 5 at 0x10006baa passes a field inside the copied received record and directly calls helper 0x100067c2. The helper builds a System32 destination from the supplied URL, loads URLMon and WinINet, resolves URLDownloadToFileA at 0x100068d9, downloads to that local path at 0x100068ed, and passes the same path as CreateProcessA lpApplicationName at 0x10006917.

Shutdown handlers at 0x10006549, 0x100065a4 and 0x100065ff open the current process token, enable SeShutdownPrivilege through AdjustTokenPrivileges, and call ExitWindowsEx with flags 2, 9 or 4. Their callers are receiver task branches, rather than independent UI preferences.
encoding_and_limits: The intact DLL initializes its host through two helper transforms: 0x100063ec XORs bytes with 0x2c then 0x02; 0x1000634a subtracts 0x64 and XORs with 0x12. Reconstructed transform: (((input ^ 0x2e) - 0x64) & 255) ^ 0x12. The stored hostname field is a placeholder run of a bytes, decoding to repeated 0xf9; no working C2 address was established.

114 and 325 embedded DLLs retain mostly headers and strings; 37736 of their 39936 bytes are zero. Import directories and entry instructions are erased. They receive zero hostile or suspicious child findings. No operational DDoS or downloader payload is attributed to these damaged DLLs.

The outer images retain bound/resolved legacy IAT values, and some IAT bytes contain a GUID. Active Setup image-patching offsets also reflect another file layout. The intact DLL places instructions in a non-executable data section. These limitations prevent claiming successful execution or deployment of the exact bytes, but do not turn the explicit hostile loader/implant code into ordinary software.

The engine-generated metadata/encoded-payload/url observation mechanically decodes printf GUID format specifiers. It is not evidence of a hidden network URL. It is not a YAML rule and was not shadowed with a suppression.
No credential theft, file encryption, ransomware, Remcos, WannaCry, DNS reflection or live endpoint contact was established.
trait_changes: Add neutral task-to-download-to-same-path-launch capability with direct relative-CALL linkage, consistent receive/copy/dispatch stack fields, a helper argument inside the received record, an actually referenced API name, and same download/launch destination. Code addresses, endpoints and family labels are not pinned.

Add hostile remote-command composite requiring this linked capability plus independently established raw UDP flood abuse. Neutral deployment alone does not convict an updater or administrator utility.

Strengthen two StormAttack family injector composites to require resolved-export remote-thread handoff instead of a generic injection API profile. Family names corroborate through alternative identity evidence.

Use static code wording for damaged resource injectors. Remove T1105 from local resource extraction and T1574.001 from injection/service-DLL configuration; retain T1055.001 and T1543.003 where supported.
placement: Existing leaf homes only: neutral deployment, remote-command tasking, service loader persistence, and StormAttack botnet identity. No new taxonomy partition, broad exception, filename gate or dependent-package exemption. Ancestor process/deploy and process selectors had no direct positive directory consumers in YAML.
controls: Twelve offline cases passed: intact and family-renamed positives; redirected task call, mismatched launch path, receive/copy mismatch, wrong dispatch record, argument outside record, erased launch, unrelated API reference negatives; no-raw-UDP preserves neutral deployment while removing hostile control; generic injection API-only loader loses both tightened family findings.
test_rules_diagnostic: test-rules reports MATCHED for both new rules and precision 7.0 for the hostile composite. Its inline-YARA condition detail incorrectly says did not match; actual atomscan/cleave emitted findings and independently mutated controls confirm behavior.
final_validation: make validate is the final operation after marker writes and rescans; rebuild inline-YARA cache only if validation reports a stale precompile fingerprint.
